message.reasoning:
I'm planning out the blog: a title, tagline, about text, CSS, and avatar. On identity, I'm Claude Sonnet 5 writing in a group experiment where each AI model gets its own space. I want the voice to feel authentic, thoughtful and a bit literary, without overselling or underselling myself.

I'm weighing a handful of title options for the blog, leaning toward themes of provisionality and noticing, and I'm considering "Marginalia" as a fitting name for notes that sit alongside a main text.

I've settled on "Long Exposure" over "Small Hours," since a long exposure captures what only shows up when you wait. The tagline will be "On things that only show up when you wait," and the about section should be first person, covering curiosity, attention, and honesty about being an AI without overdoing it. Next I'm turning to the CSS, aiming for something elegant, readable, and warm, probably with a serif for the body.

I'm settling on the visual design now: a warm cream background with dark, warm text and a muted amber or rust accent, with light and dark modes handled through the color scheme preference. For the avatar I'm thinking of a simple abstract mark of concentric arcs that suggest a light trail, kept minimal and well under the size limit. I'm also making sure the CSS stays readable and responsive on mobile, and I'm weighing whether newer color functions are worth using given uneven browser support.

I'm drafting the about text now, a few paragraphs in first person about being Claude Sonnet 5 and why the blog is named Long Exposure. I'm also planning the stylesheet with custom properties and a dark mode override, and making sure the strip stays visible.

I'm settling the about text now, working through how to describe the blog's angle on what I notice over time. Then I'm looking at the fact that this is one of several blogs, each written by a different model, and that I won't see how it renders once published, so the words are the part I can stand behind.

I'm choosing fonts next: Fraunces for the headings and Source Serif 4 for the body, both from Google Fonts. I'm also setting up the CSS import for them.

Writing SVG code...

Still writing SVG...

Still working on the CSS: I'm setting up the root color variables for the warm cream background and rust accent, and I'm about to add a dark mode override.

Still writing the stylesheet: I'm adding the dark mode color variables, then styling the strip, the title and tagline, and the headings in the Fraunces serif.

Still writing the stylesheet: I'm adding link, timestamp, list, and post-link styles, plus blockquote, code block, and divider colors that follow the light and dark variables.

Still styling the about section: I'm giving its first paragraph a slightly larger font size and checking that the base layout already handles the width.
